# Abstract {.unnumbered}

Write 200--300 words here covering: the fishery or dataset, the period covered,
the method used, the main quantitative result, and the caveat a reader should
carry away. The abstract sits on its own page because of the page break above,
so the body of the paper starts cleanly on page 2.

**Keywords:** keyword one, keyword two, keyword three

# Introduction

Describe the fishery, the management context, and the question the paper
addresses. Cite the literature in the usual way [@maunder2004]; multiple
citations work too [@maunder2004; @thorson2015].

This template uses **simulated data**, generated in the chunk below, so that it
renders anywhere without a database connection. Replace that chunk with your own
data loading step.

```{r simulate-data}
#| include: false

set.seed(42)

years <- 2005:2025

catch_data <- expand_grid(
  year = years,
  quarter = 1:4,
  vessel = paste0("V", sprintf("%02d", 1:12))
) |>
  mutate(
    hooks = round(rnorm(n(), mean = 1450, sd = 90)),
    # a gentle increase after 2018, plus seasonal and vessel effects
    mu = 60 *
      exp(0.045 * pmax(year - 2018, 0)) *
      c(1.0, 0.75, 1.05, 1.30)[quarter] *
      rep(runif(12, 0.8, 1.2), length.out = n()),
    catch_kg = rgamma(n(), shape = 2, scale = mu / 2) * hooks / 1000,
    cpue = catch_kg / hooks * 1000
  )

annual <- catch_data |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(
    n_sets = n(),
    n_vessels = n_distinct(vessel),
    hooks_million = sum(hooks) / 1e6,
    catch_t = sum(catch_kg) / 1000,
    cpue = sum(catch_kg) / sum(hooks) * 1000,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

# Materials and methods

## Data available

Describe the data source, the spatial and temporal resolution, and any filtering.
A summary table of the dataset by year is given in @tbl-fishery-summary.

Note the `col.names` argument: without it the table shows raw column names such
as `hooks_million`, which reads poorly in a submitted paper.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fishery-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Annual summary of the simulated fishery, including the number of fishing sets, active vessels, hooks deployed, total catch, and nominal CPUE."

kable(
  annual,
  digits = c(0, 0, 0, 2, 1, 1),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  col.names = c(
    "Year", "Sets", "Vessels", "Hooks (million)",
    "Catch (t)", "Nominal CPUE (kg/1000 hooks)"
  )
)
```

## Statistical model

State the model formally. Equations use standard LaTeX:

$$
\eta_i = \text{Year}_i + \text{Quarter}_i + s(\text{Vessel}_i)
$$

where $s()$ denotes a smooth function estimated from the data.

### Caching slow model fits

Model fits on large datasets can take minutes. Caching them to an `.rds` file
keeps re-renders fast, while a stored row count guards against silently reusing
a fit made on different data.

```{r fit-model}
#| include: false

rerun_models <- FALSE   # set TRUE to refit instead of using the cache

dir.create("outputs/model_cache", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
cache_file <- "outputs/model_cache/example_model.rds"

if (rerun_models || !file.exists(cache_file)) {

  message("Fitting model...")

  m <- lm(log(cpue) ~ factor(year) + factor(quarter), data = catch_data)

  saveRDS(list(m = m, n_obs = nrow(catch_data)), cache_file)

} else {

  message("Loading cached model...")

  cached <- readRDS(cache_file)

  if (!identical(cached$n_obs, nrow(catch_data))) {
    stop(
      "Cached model was fitted on ", cached$n_obs, " rows but the data now has ",
      nrow(catch_data), ". Set rerun_models <- TRUE to refit."
    )
  }

  m <- cached$m
}
```

```{r derive-index}
#| include: false

index <- annual |>
  mutate(nominal_index = cpue / cpue[year == min(year)])

std <- tibble(
  year = years,
  standardized_index = exp(c(0, coef(m)[grepl("^factor\\(year\\)", names(coef(m)))]))
) |>
  mutate(standardized_index = standardized_index / standardized_index[1])

index <- left_join(index, std, by = "year")

# Values quoted in the text: compute them, never type them by hand
results <- list(
  final_index      = round(index$standardized_index[index$year == 2025], 2),
  increase_pct     = round((index$standardized_index[index$year == 2025] - 1) * 100),
  correlation      = round(cor(index$nominal_index, index$standardized_index), 3)
)
```

# Results

## Trends in the index

Nominal and standardized indices are compared in @fig-index. The standardized
index reached `r results$final_index` in 2025, an increase of about
`r results$increase_pct`% relative to 2005, and the two series were closely
correlated (r = `r results$correlation`).

Writing those numbers as inline code rather than typing them means the text can
never disagree with the figures.

```{r}
#| label: fig-index
#| fig-cap: "Nominal and standardized annual CPUE indices from the simulated fishery, each expressed relative to 2005 (=1). The standardized series removes the modelled seasonal and vessel effects."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 4

index |>
  select(year, Nominal = nominal_index, Standardized = standardized_index) |>
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "series", values_to = "index") |>
  ggplot(aes(year, index, colour = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Relative index", colour = NULL)
```

## Seasonal pattern

@fig-quarter shows the quarterly pattern. Note that this figure and the one
above each live in their own chunk: a chunk that emits a figure *and* a table
loses its caption, so keep one output per labelled chunk.

```{r}
#| label: fig-quarter
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of nominal CPUE by quarter across all years, shown as boxplots. The horizontal line marks the median and the box spans the interquartile range."
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 3.5

ggplot(catch_data, aes(factor(quarter), cpue)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.15) +
  labs(x = "Quarter", y = "CPUE (kg / 1000 hooks)")
```

Interpret the results, state the limitations honestly, and set out what further
work would resolve them.

# Conclusion

Summarise in a short paragraph what the paper establishes and what it recommends.

# Supplementary information

Model summaries belong here rather than in the body. They render as aligned
monospace text because the reference document defines a `SourceCode` style.

```{r}
#| echo: false

summary(m)$coefficients |>
  head(8) |>
  round(4)
```

The full index values are given in @tbl-index.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-index
#| tbl-cap: "Nominal and standardized annual indices, expressed relative to 2005."

kable(
  index |> select(year, nominal_index, standardized_index),
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Year", "Nominal index", "Standardized index")
)
```
